**Conversation Overview**

This conversation documents Session 19 of an ongoing computational physics project called "Löwdin," a multi-session effort to derive atomic orbital energy observables (ionization potentials, entrant binding energies, level-to-level gaps) from first principles using a single physical constant (c = 137.035999) with no empirical fitting constants. The project uses a strict protocol (§H, Zeno structure) requiring archive verification, gate checks, and written predictions before any computation run. The person acts as ruling authority ("M"), directing which investigations to open, in what order, and when results are ready for the writing phase.

Session 19 opened by verifying the HANDOFF-18 archive (297/297 files, no foreign artefacts), rebuilding the runtime (three compiled C kernels), and passing all five standing gates before any new work began. The person's ruling was that all three bridge-18 items — (1′) spin-polarised transition-state re-probe of Ce IV/Pr V/Ra II/Sr II corridor residues, (3) analysis of the mixed-sign 4f scatter, and (2) spin-orbit level term for Lr I and the 5d edge — needed to be completed in writability order. Claude ran them in the sequence (1′)→(3)→(2), with written predictions before each run. Key findings: the TS-pol-SR object closed all four measured corridor residues to within 0.03 Ha (Sr II reclassified as an object fault rather than a physics residue); the mixed-sign 4f scatter was confirmed as the Hund-II multiplet coordinate using Slater integrals F^k derived from the project's own 4f orbital (Racah ratios F4/F2 = 0.62, F6/F2 = 0.45 reproduced without input); and first-order spin-orbit perturbation theory derived the Lr I 7p < 6d ground-state ordering (scalar gap +0.010 → −0.008 Ha), confirming the Eliav/Sato result. The 5d edge (~0.025 Ha shallow, uniform La→Gd→Lu) remained open after all three treatments.

The person's closing ruling was explicit: the project is not ready to write, and a true Löwdin solution does not leave room for an obstruction — the next step is to define and then derive the 5d edge. Claude responded by decomposing the edge along the full object chain from banked rows (t5, t7b, t7c, t7c_pol, t7c_so), establishing that the residual enters entirely at the scalar-relativistic step (SR shifts 5d removal energy +0.027→+0.044 Ha on both TS and ΔSCF objects, growing with Z, while pol and SO recover only ~0.010–0.015 Ha), and banking four ordered derivation candidates — (a) relativistic correction to local exchange (MacDonald-Vosko factor), (b) 6s² relaxation under SR in the TS vs ΔSCF split, (c) tail convention −(q−½)/r rule-out, (d) first-order SO on 4f for the Dy 0.017 Ha residual — for the next session, with instructions that predictions must be written before any run and that rulings on ordering are M's. The session closed at ~82% context per §H.10 protocol. The rebuilt HANDOFF-19 archive (316/316 verified, sha 99cea7f8a7cd0d5f) was produced as output, with R 1701–1808 owed to the writing chat when M rules it open.
